hero.headline: Supreme Court upholds FCC fines against AT&T and Verizon for selling customer location data
hero.body:
The Supreme Court has ruled 8-1 against AT&T and Verizon in a case challenging the Federal Communications Commission's power to impose penalties for mishandling customer location information. The decision affirms the agency's ability to levy fines through its internal regulatory process without triggering constitutional protections for jury trials.

The dispute centered on whether the FCC's administrative penalty system violated the companies' Seventh Amendment rights. AT&T and Verizon argued that financial sanctions for violations should require a jury trial rather than proceed through the agency's in-house proceedings. The justices rejected this challenge, upholding the FCC's enforcement framework.

The case involved both carriers' actions in allowing third parties to access sensitive location data without proper safeguards. The FCC determined that the companies had failed to implement adequate protections before sharing this information, prompting the agency to pursue enforcement action and impose fines.

The Supreme Court's decision represents a significant outcome for regulatory enforcement and privacy advocates seeking to hold telecommunications companies accountable for their data practices. Location information reveals highly personal details about individuals, including their homes, workplaces, places of worship, and medical facilities. By backing the FCC's administrative penalty system, the court strengthens the agency's ability to enforce meaningful consequences without the delays associated with jury trials.

The ruling also has broader implications for federal agencies' enforcement capabilities. It establishes that administrative penalties for telecommunications violations do not automatically trigger jury trial requirements under the Constitution, allowing regulators to proceed with enforcement actions more efficiently.

For AT&T and Verizon, the decision closes off a legal strategy that could have limited federal oversight of their data practices. Both companies must now pay the fines originally assessed by the FCC. The case sets precedent for future regulatory actions involving telecommunications companies and customer privacy protections.

The decision comes as regulators and lawmakers have increased focus on how telecommunications companies handle customer data. Location information has proven particularly sensitive because of its ability to reveal intimate details about individuals' lives and movements. The FCC's enforcement action against these carriers reflected growing concerns about third-party access to such data.

The 8-1 vote indicates strong consensus among the justices on the scope of the FCC's regulatory authority, with only one justice dissenting from the majority opinion. This overwhelming support for the agency's enforcement framework suggests the court sees administrative penalty systems as legitimate regulatory tools that do not violate constitutional protections.

The ruling also comes during the Trump administration's tenure and represents a victory for the FCC's regulatory authority during that period.

cards.headline: Zelensky Proposes Direct Talks With Putin to End War
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president wrote an open letter to his Russian counterpart suggesting face-to-face negotiations.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a public letter, marking the first time since Russia's 2022 invasion that he has addressed the Russian leader directly in this manner.

In the letter, Zelensky proposed meeting in a neutral third country and argued that only direct engagement between Ukraine and Russia could bring the war to an end. The message mixed diplomatic overtures with pointed criticism of Putin's 26-year tenure in power, suggesting that age is taking a toll on the Russian leader. Zelensky also boasted about recent Ukrainian military strikes on St. Petersburg.

According to the letter, Zelensky emphasized that while Ukrainians maintain their resolve, most Russians have grown weary of the conflict and are ready for peace. The proposal comes at a time when the United States has directed diplomatic attention elsewhere, potentially creating an opening for bilateral discussions between the two nations.

The offer represents a shift in approach from Zelensky, blending diplomatic proposals with direct criticism of his adversary. The timing coincides with mounting pressure across Europe for greater involvement in any future peace negotiations. European leaders have emphasized that no discussions about Ukraine should occur without Kyiv's participation, as they fear being sidelined from talks that could shape the continent's security.

On the Russian side, the Kremlin has proposed that former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder could serve as a mediator. However, European officials have rejected this suggestion. Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, stated that allowing Russia to appoint a negotiator on Europe's behalf would be unwise. She noted that Schröder's extensive background as a lobbyist for Russian energy companies, including work on Nord Stream pipelines and positions at Rosneft, makes him unsuitable as an impartial mediator.

German officials echoed these concerns. Germany's Europe Minister Gunther Krichbaum said Schröder has not demonstrated neutrality and remains heavily influenced by Putin. Estonia's Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated that Schröder would not represent Europe's interests.

Meanwhile, Russia continues to demand that Ukraine withdraw from the eastern Donbas region as a precondition for serious negotiations. Ukraine has flatly rejected any unilateral withdrawal from its territory. Both armies are showing signs of exhaustion while sustaining heavy casualties and conducting strikes on each other's energy infrastructure.

Analysts suggest that a diplomatic breakthrough remains unlikely in the near term. Germany's Defense Minister Boris Pistorius suggested that Putin's recent peace remarks may be a strategic deception designed to weaken Western resolve and divert attention from Russian military weaknesses rather than a genuine indication of willingness to negotiate.

cards.headline: House passes Ukraine aid package as 18 Republicans break with Trump
cards.teaser: The House passed legislation authorizing funding for military aid to Ukraine and sanctions on Russia on Thursday, with 18 Republicans and one independent joinin.
cards.body:
The House passed legislation Thursday to aid Ukraine and impose sanctions on Russia, with a 226-195 vote that included 18 Republicans crossing party lines. The measure represents the chamber's second major foreign policy break with Trump this week, following a war powers resolution on Iran the day before.

Republican leaders had opposed the bill, warning it would undermine their own negotiation efforts. The vote demonstrates impatience among some House members with Trump's approach to the conflict and reveals a divide within the GOP over Ukraine policy and the scope of American support.

cards.headline: Senate advances $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
cards.teaser: The Senate moved toward passing a budget reconciliation package funding immigration enforcement agencies after a series of amendment votes.
cards.body:
The Senate began a voting marathon on Thursday as it worked toward passing a $70 billion budget reconciliation package that would fund immigration enforcement agencies. Lawmakers considered multiple amendments during the process, with vulnerable Republicans breaking with their party on some votes.

Senate Republicans defeated an amendment sponsored by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer of New York by a vote of 49 to 50. The amendment would have prohibited the Department of Justice from establishing a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. Senator Susan Collins of Maine cast her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote during the proceedings, voting for a Democratic motion to send the package back to the Judiciary Committee.

cards.headline: Trump directs $700 million into coal using wartime powers as energy costs rise
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that he is directing $700 million in federal investment into the coal industry using wartime presidential authority. The move represents an escalation of his administration's efforts to revive America's declining coal sector.

Trump invoked the Defense Production Act, a Cold War-era statute designed to accelerate industrial output during national emergencies, to provide grants to coal-fired power plants and mining operations across the country. "Today, we're taking historic action to bring down the price of energy and the cost of living for all Americans with the power of clean, beautiful coal," Trump said at a White House press conference.

The $700 million investment will protect 14 coal plants and 42 coal mines, while also funding construction of two new coal plants and one large export terminal. The new export facility will be built in Oakland, California, and an existing facility in Maryland will be restarted. Coal plants in 10 states will remain operational through the funding: West Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, Indiana, Tennessee, Arkansas, Arizona, Oklahoma, North Dakota and Wisconsin. Trump noted that all 10 of these states voted for him in recent elections. The two new plants will be constructed in Alaska and West Virginia.

The coal industry has welcomed the announcement. Rich Nolan, chief executive of the National Mining Association, said the investment will help the US meet surging electricity demand driven by the artificial intelligence sector. "Coal generation shields consumers from the impacts of volatile energy prices and supply challenges," he said.

Environmental groups have strongly criticized the decision. Patrick Drupp, climate policy director of the Sierra Club, called it "disgusting and reprehensible" and said the funding betrays Trump's promises to lower energy costs. "This handout betrays everything Donald Trump promised and only serves his big coal buddies," Drupp said. Kit Kennedy, a senior climate campaigner at the Natural Resources Defense Council, questioned the investment's logic. "What's next, a taxpayer bailout to build new phone booths?" he asked.

Coal remains the most carbon-intensive fossil fuel and a leading contributor to climate change. Research estimates that air pollution from coal plants caused approximately 460,000 deaths in the US between 1999 and 2020. The coal industry has faced decades of decline, with US coal production now less than half of 2008 levels as natural gas and renewable energy sources have become cheaper alternatives.

Trump has long championed coal's revival, even creating a mascot called Coalie to promote the fuel. The administration has also dismantled environmental rules limiting toxins from coal plants and forced ratepayers to subsidize aging facilities. Despite these efforts, employment in coal has declined by more than 90 over the past century, with more Americans now working at Waffle Houses than in coal mining.

cards.headline: Former Trump adviser John Bolton to plead guilty in classified documents case
cards.teaser: John Bolton has reached a plea deal to resolve charges related to mishandling sensitive national security information.
cards.body:
John Bolton, who served as national security adviser under President Trump before becoming a prominent critic of the administration, has reached a plea agreement in a case charging him with mishandling classified documents. The deal, subject to court approval, allows Bolton to plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information.

The Justice Department filed charges against Bolton in 2025 as part of proceedings against the president's critics. Bolton served as national security adviser from April 2018 to September 2019 before departing the administration.

cards.headline: Ohio State University settles sexual abuse lawsuits for $100 million
cards.body:
Ohio State University's board of trustees has approved a $100 million settlement to resolve lawsuits filed by survivors of sexual abuse perpetrated by Richard Strauss, a physician who treated students at the institution for two decades.

Strauss worked at Ohio State from 1978 to 1998 and sexually abused male students who sought medical treatment. An independent investigation commissioned by the university in 2018 determined that Strauss had abused at least 177 male students. The investigation also revealed that university officials had received complaints about Strauss as early as 1979 but failed to take action to stop him. Strauss died in 2005.

As of February, Ohio State had already reached settlement agreements totaling more than $60 million with more than 100 survivors. More than 100 additional plaintiffs had litigation still pending at that time. The new $100 million settlement represents the final resolution of the formal litigation process, with all but one of the Strauss survivors agreeing to settle with the university.

The university stated that none of the settlements involved taxpayer funds, tuition money, or restricted donor funds, according to reporting by the National Public Radio affiliate WOSU.

The Ohio State case emerged during a challenging period for the institution. The university faced significant backlash surrounding former trustee and prominent alumnus Les Wexner, a retail mogul with a well-documented relationship with late financier Jeffrey Epstein. Following Wexner's congressional testimony about his connection to the disgraced Epstein in February, growing calls emerged for the university to remove Wexner's name from campus and health system facilities.

The settlement came shortly after Ohio State's president, Walter "Ted" Carter Jr., resigned following disclosure of an inappropriate relationship. Carter, who had led the university since 2024, stated that he "made a mistake in allowing inappropriate access to Ohio State leadership." The board accepted his resignation after determining he "had an inappropriate relationship with someone seeking public resources to support her personal business." Board Chair John Zeiger said the board was "surprised and disappointed" to learn of the matter and emphasized that it "takes the situation and its potential impact on the university very seriously."

Carter had previously served as president of the University of Nebraska from 2020 to 2023. He succeeded Kristina Johnson, who resigned from Ohio State in November 2022.

Ohio State has implemented new policies and procedures aimed at preventing similar abuse in the future, including enhanced reporting mechanisms and mandatory training for staff who work with students. The university has apologized to survivors and acknowledged that it failed to protect students during the Strauss period.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Ceasefire Between Israel and Lebanon
cards.teaser: Hezbollah rejected a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon that the United States announced Wednesday night, with the group's leader calling the deal a.
cards.body:
Hezbollah rejected a ceasefire agreement announced Wednesday between Israel and Lebanon, with the group's leader characterizing the deal as surrender. The U.S.-brokered truce was negotiated between the Israeli and Lebanese governments without Hezbollah's participation, a significant obstacle to implementing any halt in hostilities.

Fighting continued despite the announced ceasefire, with Israeli and Hezbollah forces exchanging strikes. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when struck by mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon. Israel announced it would maintain ground operations in southern Lebanon despite the agreed ceasefire.

cards.headline: Missing Sherpa Guide Found Alive on Everest After Week-Long Search
cards.teaser: Hillary Dawa Sherpa was discovered crawling toward base camp after his family had begun funeral rites.
cards.body:
Hillary Dawa Sherpa was found alive after going missing on Mount Everest, crawling toward Base Camp six days later. A cleaning crew spotted him as he made his way down the mountain. His family had already begun funeral rites, believing he had died.

Climber Chris Thrall recounted losing contact with Dawa Sherpa during their ascent at high altitude. The guide's survival alone in the harsh conditions of Everest's upper reaches represents a remarkable rescue from one of the world's most dangerous environments.

cards.headline: Ireland Moves to Strengthen Military Amid European Defense Concerns
cards.teaser: The government says it is working to address gaps in its armed forces as worries grow about Russian threats.
cards.body:
Ireland is working to bulk up its military capabilities after being identified as a weak link in European defense. The Irish government announced efforts to plug gaps in its armed forces, which have historically been shaped by the country's tradition of neutrality.

Concern has risen across Europe over threats from Russia, prompting even traditionally neutral countries to reassess their defense postures. Ireland's military has long maintained a limited profile in line with its neutral status, but officials now acknowledge the need for greater capability. The move reflects a broader shift in European security thinking as countries previously outside military alliances reconsider their positions.

cards.headline: US to Deploy Flies and Dogs Against Screwworm Outbreak
cards.teaser: The flesh-eating insect has appeared in America for the first time since 1966, raising concerns in southern states.
cards.body:
The United States is responding to a screwworm outbreak using sterile flies and detection dogs to contain the invasive parasite. The insect has been found in America for the first time since 1966, marking a significant return after decades of successful eradication efforts.

Screwworms pose a serious threat to livestock and human health, as they infest open wounds. The outbreak has emerged as a growing concern in the southern United States, prompting swift action from officials to prevent further spread of the flesh-eating parasite.

cards.headline: Mangrove Forests Stage Comeback After Decades of Destruction
cards.teaser: The coastal ecosystems are recovering globally, providing benefits for communities and climate.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests around the world are experiencing a surprise recovery after being heavily destroyed by human activity. These coastal wetland ecosystems are now expanding again in multiple locations.

The resurgence of mangrove forests benefits both coastal communities and climate action. These forests act as natural shields against storm surges and flooding, while also capturing and storing carbon dioxide. They also function as breeding grounds for fish and other marine life, which helps sustain local fishing communities and supports overall biodiversity.

cards.headline: Trump's White House Ballroom Plan Doubles in Size and Cost
cards.teaser: The proposed renovation has grown significantly over the past year, marking the biggest change to the building in decades.
cards.body:
A proposed White House ballroom has grown significantly in both size and cost over the past year, representing the biggest renovation to the executive mansion in decades. BBC Verify tracked how the project's scope expanded substantially from its initial announcement.

The plan has faced political opposition. Senate Republicans moved to block $1 billion in funding for the ballroom as part of a bill meant to fund immigration agencies, delaying the legislation over disputes about the project's costs and other priorities.

cards.headline: Murder charge dismissed against Arkansas sheriff candidate who shot daughter's alleged abuser
cards.teaser: A judge has dismissed the murder charge against Aaron Spencer, a candidate for Lonoke County sheriff.
cards.body:
Aaron Spencer, a candidate for sheriff in Lonoke County, Arkansas, will no longer face murder charges after a judge dismissed the case. Spencer had been charged with murder following an incident in which he shot and killed a man he believed had abused his daughter.

Court documents confirm the dismissal, though the specific reasoning behind the judge's decision has not been detailed in available reports. Spencer was running for sheriff at the time of the incident and the subsequent legal proceedings. The case attracted significant attention because of Spencer's law enforcement candidacy and the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

cards.headline: California's ballot counting process draws criticism as results remain incomplete
cards.teaser: California continues to count ballots from its primary election, prompting renewed criticism of the state's vote-tallying timeline.
cards.body:
California's election results could take weeks or even a month to finalize, making the state's counting process significantly slower than many others. The extended timeline has drawn criticism from observers questioning why the process takes so long.

The delay stems from California's policies allowing mail-in ballots postmarked by election day to be counted if they arrive days after voting ends. The state also processes provisional ballots and conducts verification procedures that lengthen the overall counting period. Election officials say the extended process reflects the state's commitment to accuracy rather than any problems with the electoral system.

cards.headline: George Santos threatened reporter covering federal investigations into his activities
cards.teaser: The former congressman made a violent threat against an NPR reporter after coverage of new federal probes.
cards.body:
Federal authorities are investigating whether former Congressman George Santos engaged in insider trading through bets placed on Kalshi, a prediction market website. Santos allegedly wagered on whether he would attend Trump's State of the Union address in February, according to reporting by NPR.

After NPR published its investigation into the federal probe, Santos made a violent threat against the reporter who broke the story. Santos later denied making the threat, contradicting NPR's account of events. The investigation represents additional legal scrutiny for Santos, who was previously expelled from Congress following revelations about fabrications in his background and federal charges related to campaign finance violations.

cards.headline: House passes Ukraine aid package over objections from Republican leadership
cards.teaser: The House of Representatives approved military aid for Ukraine and sanctions on Russia despite opposition from GOP leaders.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives passed legislation Thursday to provide aid to Ukraine and impose sanctions on Russia's economy, voting 226-195. About 18 Republicans joined Democrats to support the measure, defying opposition from GOP leadership who warned the bill could undermine ongoing negotiations.

The vote marks the second major foreign policy break between the House and former President Trump in a week. The previous day, the chamber approved a war powers resolution to halt U.S. military action against Iran. The divisions highlight ongoing disagreements within the Republican Party over foreign policy direction.

cards.headline: Trump White House ballroom expansion doubles in size and cost
cards.teaser: Plans for a new ballroom at the White House have grown significantly larger and more expensive over the past year.
cards.body:
The White House ballroom expansion has grown substantially since initial plans were announced a year ago, with both its physical footprint and budget doubling. BBC Verify has identified this as the most significant structural change to the White House in decades.

The project has been a priority for the Trump administration, though the ballooning costs have drawn scrutiny. Senate Republicans have moved to block $1 billion in funding for the ballroom as part of a larger bill affecting immigration agencies.

cards.headline: S&P blocks SpaceX from early entry to benchmark index
cards.teaser: The index provider reaffirmed existing rules after speculation that it might fast-track SpaceX following its planned public offering.
cards.body:
S&P has declined to make exceptions to its standard eligibility rules for SpaceX ahead of the company's anticipated initial public offering. The index provider maintained its existing requirements, which call for companies to establish a track record of financial stability across multiple quarters before joining its benchmark index.

The decision puts SpaceX on the same timeline as other companies seeking inclusion, despite expectations that S&P might create a special pathway for a mega IPO of this scale. The ruling applies to other large prospective offerings as well.

cards.headline: Wall Street banks prepare to pitch SpaceX offering as largest IPO ever
cards.teaser: Jamie Dimon is planning to personally pitch investors on the SpaceX initial public offering as banks prepare for huge fees.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for what would be the largest initial public offering in history, with a stock market launch targeted for June 12. The offering could raise up to $75 billion, potentially valuing the rocket company at $1.77 trillion.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is among top Wall Street executives personally involved in pitching the deal to investors. Banks are positioning themselves to collect substantial underwriting fees from the blockbuster offering. If successful, the IPO could make founder Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.

cards.headline: Dow gains more than 500 points while Nasdaq dips after Broadcom earnings
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted gains while the Nasdaq declined following earnings from chipmaker Broadcom.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 500 points while the Nasdaq fell following Broadcom's earnings announcement. Healthcare and financial stocks led the Dow to a fresh record, offsetting weakness elsewhere in the market.

Broadcom's results unsettled the artificial intelligence sector, prompting investors to sell technology stocks and major Wall Street tech names. The pullback extended globally, with Asian tech stocks also declining in the wake of the chipmaker's earnings.

cards.headline: Anthropic co-founder warns AI may need brakes as systems develop without human input
cards.teaser: Jack Clark said artificial intelligence could reach a point where it develops independently, raising concerns about control mechanisms.
cards.body:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark has cautioned that artificial intelligence requires safeguards as systems advance rapidly. Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Clark expressed concern that AI could eventually develop without direct human guidance, potentially making humans the limiting factor in technological progress.

The company has highlighted the accelerating pace of AI capabilities, noting that Claude now authors 80 percent of its new production code. Anthropic has called for a global pause on AI development and raised alarms about the risks posed by self-improving systems operating beyond human oversight.

cards.headline: Google conducting layoffs in cloud division
cards.teaser: The technology company is quietly cutting staff in its cloud business unit.
cards.body:
Google is laying off employees in its cloud division. The cuts are being conducted quietly as the company adjusts its workforce in the competitive cloud computing market.

The cloud division has been a key growth area for Google as it competes with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. The layoffs come as technology companies continue to adjust staffing levels following rapid expansion in previous years. Google has not disclosed the number of positions affected by the reductions.

cards.headline: Hinge executive says single adults need AI to initiate dating app conversations
cards.teaser: The dating app's boss cited loneliness and lack of confidence as challenges for young adults seeking relationships.
cards.body:
Hinge boss Jackie Jantos has highlighted loneliness and lack of confidence as key barriers preventing young adults in their twenties from making the first move on dating apps. According to Jantos, artificial intelligence could help address these challenges by assisting users with initiating conversations.

The remarks indicate that dating platforms are considering AI tools to support users during the early stages of online interaction, reflecting how technology companies are adapting to evolving social behaviors and user needs.

cards.headline: Meta added facial recognition code for smart glasses to millions of phones
cards.teaser: Code discovered in Meta's AI app could enable facial recognition features for the company's smart glasses.
cards.body:
Wired reported finding code for an unreleased facial recognition feature embedded in Meta's AI application. The code has been distributed to millions of phones through the app, though the feature is not currently active for users.

The discovery raises privacy concerns about Meta's plans for its smart glasses technology. Facial recognition capabilities in wearable devices could allow real-time identification of people in public settings. The finding has prompted a lawsuit and leaked internal memos about the feature's development.

cards.headline: Anthropic revenue reaches $47 billion annually ahead of planned IPO
cards.teaser: The AI company's annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced that its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, a dramatic increase from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company is preparing for an initial public offering.

Co-founder Daniela Amodei has addressed skepticism about returns on artificial intelligence investments as Anthropic experiences rapid expansion. The company's growth trajectory positions it among the fastest-growing AI firms, though the sustainability of such acceleration will be tested in the market ahead of the IPO.

cards.headline: New app blocks advertisements across iPhone and Mac applications
cards.teaser: Filtr uses a feature in the latest Apple software to block ads from loading inside apps, including web browsers.
cards.body:
Filtr, a privacy tool for iPhones, iPads, and Macs, can now block ads from loading inside applications across the platform. The app works thanks to a new feature available in the latest Apple operating system software.

Unlike traditional ad blockers that target only web browsers like Safari, Filtr extends its capabilities to block advertisements within various apps. This represents a significant expansion in how ad blocking technology functions on Apple devices.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO plans to launch artificial intelligence laboratory
cards.teaser: Brian Chesky previously said the company has not partnered with existing large language model providers because the products were not ready.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky has announced plans to launch a new artificial intelligence laboratory. The move comes after Chesky previously explained that the company had not pursued partnerships with large language model providers because existing products did not meet its needs.

Rather than adopting third-party AI solutions, Airbnb is choosing to build its own capabilities. The new lab represents the company's commitment to developing proprietary artificial intelligence technology tailored specifically for its vacation rental platform.

cards.headline: Google Health app update addresses 16 bugs in nutrition, fitness, and sleep tracking
cards.teaser: Version 5.01 of Google Health includes fixes for issues across the app's health tracking features.
cards.body:
Google released version 5.01 of its Health app with fixes for 16 bugs affecting nutrition tracking, fitness monitoring, and sleep analysis. The update improves core features across these health categories.

Google Health is replacing the Fitbit app on smartphones as the company consolidates health tracking functions into a single platform.

cards.headline: Mangrove forests recover after decades of destruction
cards.teaser: Swampy mangrove forests are staging a comeback, offering benefits for coastal communities and climate mitigation.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests are making a comeback after suffering extensive damage from human activity. These coastal ecosystems are regenerating across multiple regions, reversing a long period of decline.

The recovery benefits both local communities and the environment. Coastal populations gain improved protection from storms and access to fisheries that depend on mangroves. The forests also support climate goals by storing carbon in their roots and soil, making their restoration valuable for addressing broader environmental challenges.

hero.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and three picks
hero.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks, marking a significant shift in the defensive landscape for both franchises.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns selected him with the first overall pick in 2017, he has accumulated 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures, and 149 tackles for loss—more than any other player during that span. In 2025, he set a single-season sacks record with 23 tackles.

Garrett had requested a trade from the Browns in 2024 after the team finished with a 3-14 record, expressing his desire to join a championship contender. Despite his trade request, he signed a four-year, $160 million extension with Cleveland that made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal included $122.8 million guaranteed and an average annual salary of $40 million.

The Browns again disappointed in 2025, finishing with a 5-12 record and missing the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Garrett was the lone Browns player to earn All-Pro recognition. The franchise subsequently fired head coach Kevin Stefanski and hired former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken.

General manager Andrew Berry said the decision came after extensive discussions about the team's future direction. "As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry stated.

To make the trade possible, the Browns and Garrett modified his contract in March, deferring option payments over the 2026-28 seasons. A payment that was originally due on March 28 was moved to near the start of the regular season.

The Rams acquired a defensive player who immediately strengthens their pass-rushing unit. They also lost to the eventual champion Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC Championship Game. The team has a history of making aggressive moves, including trading Jared Goff to acquire Matthew Stafford in 2021. Stafford led Los Angeles to a Super Bowl victory in his first season.

In return, the Browns received Verse, a 25-year-old linebacker who was the Rams' first-round pick in 2024. Verse earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors and was selected to the Pro Bowl this past season with 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss. Cleveland also received a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection.

cards.headline: Yankees slugger Aaron Judge out with stress fracture in ribs
cards.teaser: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge will miss time with a stress fracture in his ribs on his right side.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge will miss time with a stress fracture in his right rib, the New York Yankees confirmed. The injury was diagnosed after Judge had been managing what initially appeared to be a standard rib injury.

The Yankees expect Judge to return during the 2024 season, though they have not announced a specific timeline for his return. His absence removes one of baseball's most productive hitters from the Yankees' lineup during a crucial stretch of the season.

cards.headline: Formula 1 extends Las Vegas Grand Prix contract through 2037
cards.teaser: Formula 1 signed a 10-year extension to continue racing in Las Vegas through 2037.
cards.body:
Formula 1 has extended its Las Vegas Grand Prix contract for another 10 years, keeping the race on the calendar through at least 2037. The agreement renews the partnership between Formula 1 and the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix has become a prominent addition to the F1 calendar since its recent debut, solidifying its place among the sport's signature events.

cards.headline: Packers sign wide receiver Christian Watson to four-year extension
cards.teaser: The Green Bay Packers and wide receiver Christian Watson agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $110.5 million.
cards.body:
Christian Watson signed a four-year contract extension with the Green Bay Packers worth $110.5 million. The deal keeps the wide receiver in Green Bay through the 2030 season.

Watson has emerged as a key target in the Packers offense. The extension represents a significant investment by Green Bay in securing a core piece of their receiving corps for the foreseeable future.

cards.headline: Fan receives lifetime NBA ban after running onto court for selfie with Wembanyama
cards.teaser: A fan was arrested and banned for life from all NBA arenas after running onto the court during Game 1 of the NBA Finals to take a selfie with Victor Wembanyama.
cards.body:
The NBA issued lifetime bans to two fans following an incident during Game 1 of the NBA Finals. One fan ran onto the court attempting to take a selfie with San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama and was arrested.

In a separate matter, the league is investigating an interaction between New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson and fans during the fourth quarter of Wednesday night's game, which the Knicks won 105-95 over the Spurs.

cards.headline: Fever defeat Dream 83-71 in Commissioner's Cup opener
cards.teaser: Kelsey Mitchell scored 25 points as the Indiana Fever beat the Atlanta Dream 83-71 to begin their Commissioner's Cup title defense.
cards.body:
The Indiana Fever defeated the Atlanta Dream 83-71 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in the opening game of the Commissioner's Cup. Kelsey Mitchell led the Fever with 25 points, while Caitlin Clark also contributed to the victory.

The win marks a successful start to Indiana's defense of their Commissioner's Cup title. The Fever used a balanced offensive attack to pull away from Atlanta in front of their home crowd.

cards.headline: Shakira to perform at 2026 World Cup opening ceremony in Mexico
cards.teaser: Colombian pop star Shakira will perform her official World Cup song at the opening ceremony of the 2026 tournament in Mexico.
cards.body: Shakira will perform her official song for the 2026 World Cup at the tournament's opening ceremony in Mexico. The Colombian pop star's performance will take place before the first match of the competition.

hero.headline: SAG-AFTRA Members Ratify Four-Year Contract With AI Provisions
hero.teaser: The union approved a new deal with major studios that includes terms on synthetic actors and merges two pension funds.
hero.body:
SAG-AFTRA members have approved a four-year contract with major studios that introduces new rules for synthetic actors and combines the union's two separate pension systems into one. The voting results showed strong support, with 91.4 percent in favor and 8.6 percent opposed among those who cast ballots. However, turnout remained modest at 19.3 percent of all eligible members.

The new agreement addresses growing concerns about artificial intelligence in the entertainment industry by establishing specific conditions under which producers can use synthetic actors. These provisions represent a significant negotiation point between the union and studios as technology continues to reshape film and television production.

Beyond the AI protections, the contract consolidates the union's dual pension fund structure. This merger streamlines the pension system for members, combining what were previously two separate financial arrangements into a unified framework. The consolidation is expected to simplify administration and potentially improve oversight of retirement benefits for performers.

The ratification concludes a negotiation process between SAG-AFTRA and the major studios over contractual terms governing how film and television productions operate. The discussions centered on balancing the industry's desire to adopt new technology with the union's need to protect members' livelihoods and working conditions.

The strong approval margin suggests broad support for the agreement's terms among those who voted. The contract covers a four-year period, providing stability for both studios and performers as they navigate rapid technological change in the industry.

The AI provisions are particularly noteworthy given the ongoing debates throughout Hollywood about how artificial intelligence should be integrated into creative work. By establishing guidelines for synthetic actors, the contract attempts to create a framework that allows technological innovation while maintaining protections for union members.

The pension fund merger represents an important administrative change that could have long-term implications for member retirement security. By combining the two funds, the union aims to create a more efficient and potentially more sustainable pension system.

With this ratification, the union and studios have established a path forward for the next four years of cooperation. The agreement demonstrates an effort to address contemporary industry challenges while maintaining the fundamental relationship between labor and management in film and television production.

The modest turnout for the ratification vote reflects broader patterns in union voting, where participation rates often fall below 50 percent of eligible members. Nevertheless, the overwhelming support among those who did vote indicates that the negotiating team's agreement resonates with the active membership.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Stabbing at 81
cards.teaser: James Handy, an actor who appeared in Top Gun: Maverick, Jumanji, and numerous television shows over a decades-long career, was killed in a stabbing at his home.
cards.body:
James Handy, a veteran character actor with a decades-long career in film and television, was fatally stabbed Wednesday at his home in the Tarzana neighborhood of Los Angeles. He was 81. Police arrested his girlfriend's son in connection with the killing.

Handy appeared as a bartender in the blockbuster Top Gun: Maverick and had a role in Jumanji. Throughout his career, he built a steady presence in Hollywood with guest appearances on numerous television shows and work in supporting roles across both film and television productions.

cards.headline: Madonna Performs in Times Square for Pride Month
cards.teaser: The pop star debuted a new track from her Confessions II album during a public performance in New York.
cards.body:
Madonna performed in Times Square, debuting the track Love Sensation from her Confessions II album. The performance took place during Pride Month and drew crowds to the New York landmark. She straddled a speaker box and played air guitar during the set.

The appearance marked a public return to Times Square for the artist. Madonna used the performance to showcase new music while celebrating Pride Month with fans in one of the city's most visible locations.

cards.headline: Trump Cancels Freedom 250 Concerts, Plans Rally Instead
cards.teaser: The president officially canceled planned concerts on the National Mall after artist withdrawals and announced a rally as replacement programming.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump officially canceled the Freedom 250 concerts scheduled for the National Mall in Washington, D.C., after nearly all booked artists withdrew from the event. The concerts were originally designed to celebrate America's 250th anniversary.

Trump announced the concerts will be replaced with a rally featuring himself as the main attraction, along with performer Lee Greenwood. Vanilla Ice was among the few artists who had agreed to participate before the cancellation.

cards.headline: Clive Davis Released From Hospital After Respiratory Issue
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old music executive was discharged and is recovering at home after treatment in New York.
cards.body:
Music executive Clive Davis has been discharged from a New York hospital and is recuperating at home following treatment for a respiratory issue. The 94-year-old music mogul is in good spirits, according to his representative.

Davis has had a legendary career in the music industry, working with many major artists throughout his decades in the business. He is now focusing on his recovery at home.

cards.headline: Nick Bilton Named New Chief of 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The appointment follows the recent firing of three correspondents from the longtime news program.
cards.body:
Nick Bilton was named the new chief of 60 Minutes and pledged to maintain the program's independence. The appointment follows CBS News's decision to fire three correspondents from the program, including Scott Pelley.

The personnel changes have created uncertainty about the show's future. Former 60 Minutes correspondent Steve Kroft suggested the program as it has been known no longer exists following the firings. The departures have raised questions among CBS News insiders about how the broadcast will continue and what content will fill the schedule.

cards.headline: Jennifer Lopez and Brett Goldstein Star in Office Romance
cards.teaser: The workplace romantic comedy pairs Lopez as an airline CEO with Goldstein as her company lawyer.
cards.body:
Jennifer Lopez returns to Netflix with Office Romance, a workplace romantic comedy featuring her alongside Brett Goldstein, who also co-wrote the script. Lopez plays Jackie Cruz, an airline CEO, while Goldstein portrays Daniel Blanchflower, the company's new lawyer. Rather than a traditional meet-cute, their characters' first encounter happens when Cruz summons Blanchflower to her office.

Critics have noted that Lopez brings her characteristic charm to the lead role, while reviews suggest the film follows a fairly standard romantic comedy formula. However, some reviewers felt the script and Goldstein's performance lacked the spark needed to elevate the familiar workplace romance premise.

hero.headline: Senate advances $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
hero.teaser: The Senate moved toward passing a budget reconciliation package funding immigration enforcement agencies after a series of amendment votes.
hero.body:
The Senate began a voting marathon on Thursday as it worked toward passing a $70 billion budget reconciliation package that would fund immigration enforcement agencies. Lawmakers considered multiple amendments during the process, with vulnerable Republicans breaking with their party on some votes.

Senate Republicans defeated an amendment sponsored by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer of New York by a vote of 49 to 50. The amendment would have prohibited the Department of Justice from establishing a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. Senator Susan Collins of Maine cast her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote during the proceedings, voting for a Democratic motion to send the package back to the Judiciary Committee.

cards.headline: House passes Ukraine aid package as 18 Republicans break with Trump
cards.teaser: The House passed legislation authorizing funding for military aid to Ukraine and sanctions on Russia on Thursday, with 18 Republicans and one independent joinin.
cards.body:
The House passed legislation Thursday to aid Ukraine and impose sanctions on Russia, with a 226-195 vote that included 18 Republicans crossing party lines. The measure represents the chamber's second major foreign policy break with Trump this week, following a war powers resolution on Iran the day before.

Republican leaders had opposed the bill, warning it would undermine their own negotiation efforts. The vote demonstrates impatience among some House members with Trump's approach to the conflict and reveals a divide within the GOP over Ukraine policy and the scope of American support.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra advances to California governor general election
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services secretary won a spot in November's election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra, a Democrat, has advanced to California's gubernatorial general election in November, according to Decision Desk HQ's projection on Thursday. He will compete to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

The second spot in the general election remains contested between Republican Steve Hilton, a Trump-backed Fox News commentator, and Democrat Tom Steyer, a billionaire. The primary race also featured Democrats Katie Porter and Republicans Chad Bianco.

cards.headline: FCC reviews school internet subsidy program over screen time concerns
cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission announced a complete review of the $3 billion annual E-Rate program.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission is reviewing the E-Rate program, which distributes $3 billion annually to schools and libraries for internet access. FCC Chair Brendan Carr announced the review this week, driven by mounting concerns about children's screen time and its health effects.

The commission will examine the program's impact and release its findings as part of a complete review of the subsidy initiative.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. Haaland's victory positions her as the Democratic nominee heading into the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor. She previously served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign in New Mexico.

cards.headline: Trump announces Washington rally for 250th birthday celebration
cards.teaser: The president scheduled an event to commemorate America's 250th birthday after artists dropped out of a planned National Mall fair.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a rally in Washington on Thursday to mark America's 250th birthday. The event comes after several performers withdrew from plans to participate in the "Great American State Fair" on the National Mall.

According to Trump, organizers discouraged high-fee performers from participating in the celebration of the nation's semiquincentennial.

cards.headline: Trump dominates New York House debate for 12th District seat
cards.teaser: Candidates vying to replace Representative Jerry Nadler frequently referenced the president during their debate.
cards.body:
President Trump's name dominated Thursday's debate among candidates seeking to represent New York's 12th Congressional District, currently held by Rep. Jerry Nadler, a Democrat. The candidates discussed various issues with frequent references to the president throughout the discussion.

Four Democrats participated in the debate on PIX11: lawyer George Conway, Jack Schlossberg (former President Kennedy's grandson), and New York State Assemblymembers Alex Bores and Micah Lasher.
